title: KOREAN VETERANS ASSOCIATION ACT
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to establish a Korean Veterans Association to promote friendship among veterans through mutual aid, to improve the rights and interests of members, and to contribute to national development and the public interest.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 2 (Legal personality and establishment) (1) The Korean Veterans Association (hereinafter referred to as the "Veterans Association") shall be a legal entity.
  (2) The Veterans Association shall be established when it registers such establishment after preparing its articles of incorporation with approval of the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on Mar. 4, 2023>
  (3) Except as provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning legal entities shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Veterans Association.
  (4) No Veterans Association that does not comply with this Act shall be established and no entity other than the Veterans Association under this Act shall use the title "Veterans Association" or similar.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 3 (Prohibition of political activities) (1) The Veterans Association shall not engage in any political activity.
  (2) All executive officers of the main or branch offices of the Veterans Association are disqualified from serving as the representative, an executive member or a person in charge of accounting of a political party under the Political Parties Act.
  (3) If an executive officer of the main or branch office of the Veterans Association violates paragraph (2), such executive officer shall be dismissed from service.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 4 (Articles of incorporation) The articles of incorporation of the Veterans Association shall contain the following matters:
  1. Name;
  2. Location of offices;
  3. Matters pertaining to business activities;
  4. Matters pertaining to the rights and duties of members;
  5. Matters pertaining to general meetings and the board of directors;
  6. Matters pertaining to executive organs and their work responsibilities;
  7. Matters pertaining to assets, membership fees and audit;
  8. Matters pertaining to amendments to the articles of incorporation;
  9. Matters pertaining to executive officers and employees;
  10. Other matters pertaining to the operation of the Veterans Association.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 4-2 (Projects) The Veterans Association shall engage in the following projects to attain the purpose specified in Article 1: <Amended on Jul. 11, 2023>
  1. Promotion of friendship through mutual aid among members of the Veterans Association (hereinafter referred to as "member");
  2. Promotion of welfare and the rights and interests of the members;
  3. Cooperation and assistance in regional defense;
  4. Maintenance and strengthening of friendly relationship with international veterans associations;
  5. Cultivation and instilling of the spirit for defending the country;
  6. Profit-making and other incidental projects necessary for conducting the projects specified in subparagraphs 1 through 5.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 4-3 Deleted. <Jul. 11, 2023>

Article 4-4 Deleted. <Jul. 11, 2023>

Article 4-5 Deleted. <Jul. 11, 2023>

Article 4-6 Deleted. <Jul. 11, 2023>

Article 4-7 Deleted. <Jul. 11, 2023>

CHAPTER II ORGANIZATION

Article 5 (Qualifications for membership) Any of the following persons is eligible for membership: <Amended on Jun. 4, 2013; May 29, 2016>
  1. A person in reserve service after having served in the army, navy or air forces;
  2. A person who has completed his term of service after having been called up for replacement service or wartime workers service;
  3. Officer, warrant officer, noncommissioned officer or enlisted man who is retired or exempted from service, as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 6 (Organization) (1) The Veterans Association shall have a main office, City/Do branches, Si/Gun/Gu branches and Eup/Myeon/Dong branches and may, as prescribed by the articles of incorporation, have workplace branches, joint branches or other branches for employees according to the scale of place of work and overseas branches, joint branches or other branches for overseas residents according to the size of area.
  (2) The Veterans Association shall have the main office in the metropolitan area, City/Do branches in the Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan Cities, the Special Self-Governing City, Dos, and Special Self-Governing Provinces, Si/Gun/Gu branches in Sis/Guns/Gus (referring to autonomous Gus), and Eup/Myeon/Dong branches in Eups/Myeons/Dongs. <Amended on Aug. 13, 2013>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

CHAPTER III DELIBERATIVE ORGANS

Article 7 (General meeting) (1) A general meeting shall be comprised of the president, vice presidents, secretary general, directors, presidents of City/Do branches and other branches, and delegates.
  (2) The delegates under paragraph (1) shall be elected from among the members.
  (3) Necessary matters regarding the fixed number, election and terms of office of delegates under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
  (4) A general meeting shall have the power to decide important matters prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 8 (Convocation of general meeting) (1) A regular general meeting shall be called by the president once a year.
  (2) An extraordinary general meeting shall be called by the president when deemed necessary by the president or upon the request of at least 1/3 of the delegates for convocation of such meeting.
  (3) Upon receipt of delegates’ request for convocation of a meeting under paragraph (2), the president shall call such meeting within 15 days from the date such request is received.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 9 (Meeting and resolution) A resolution in a general meeting shall be made with the presence of a majority of the members and by the concurring votes of a majority of those present; provided, when it is intended to amend the articles of incorporation, the resolution shall be made with the presence of a majority of the members and by the concurring votes of at least 2/3 of those present.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 10 (Approval and reporting of resolutions) (1) If the Veterans Association intends to amend its articles of incorporation, it shall obtain approval from the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs following a resolution at a general meeting.
  (2) The Veterans Association shall report the following matters to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs following a resolution at a general meeting:
  1. Matters regarding budgets and settlement of accounts;
  2. Matters regarding business plans.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 11 (Board of directors) (1) The Veterans Association shall have a board of directors.
  (2) The board of directors shall have the power to determine the matters prescribed by the articles of incorporation and other matters delegated by general meetings.
  (3) The board of directors shall be comprised of directors.
  (4) The president and vice presidents shall be ex officio directors.
  (5) A resolution of the board of directors shall require the presence of a majority of the directors and the concurring votes of a majority of those present.
  (6) The secretary general may attend and speak at meetings of the board of directors.
  (7) If deemed impracticably difficult to call a general meeting due to any natural disaster or other urgent circumstances, the president may authorize the board of directors to act on behalf of such general meeting after obtaining approval from the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. In such cases, any resolution made by the board of directors shall be subject to approval by the next general meeting. <Amended on Mar. 4, 2023>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

CHAPTER IV EXECUTIVE ORGANS

Article 12 (Executive officers) (1) The main office of the Veterans Association shall have the president, vice presidents, secretary general, directors and auditor as executive officers.
  (2) The president, vice presidents, directors and auditor shall be elected at a general meeting, and the secretary general shall be appointed by the president; provided, when there is any unavoidable reason that makes it impossible to call a general meeting, in cases of a vacancy in the office of any director or auditor, other than the president and vice presidents, such vacancy may be filled by the board of directors. In such cases, the director or auditor elected by the board of directors shall hold office until the day before the next general meeting is held.
  (3) The president shall represent and exercise overall control over affairs of the Veterans Association, and preside over a general meeting and the board of directors.
  (4) The vice presidents shall assist the president and act on behalf of the president in the order designated in advance by the president if the president is not able to perform his or her duties for any unavoidable reason.
  (5) The secretary general shall deal with general affairs of the Veterans Association under the president’s orders and direct and supervise its staff members.
  (6) The auditor shall examine the accounts and other related affairs of the Veterans Association.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 13 (Number, terms of office of executive officers) (1) The number and terms of office of executive officers to be assigned to the main office of the Veterans Association shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
  (2) The kind, number, methods of election, and terms of office, with respect to executive officers to be assigned to various levels of branch offices, other than the main office of the Veterans Association, shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 14 (Reimbursement of actual expenses) Executive officers (excluding those subject to appointment) and delegates of the main office and branch offices of the Veterans Association shall serve without pay, but may receive reimbursement for actual expenses within the budget; provided, executive officers subject to appointment may be paid remuneration as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 15 (General affairs sections) (1) The main and branch offices of the Veterans Association may have general affairs sections and clerical workers necessary to handle their business affairs.
  (2) The general affairs sections and the maximum number and remuneration of clerical workers under paragraph (1) and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

CHAPTER V FINANCES

Article 16 (Finances) (1) The financial resources of the Veterans Association shall consist of membership fees, operational gains and other earnings.
  (2) The State and local governments may grant subsidies to the Veterans Association if deemed necessary for the operation thereof and for other purposes within budgetary limits. <Amended on May 29, 2016>
  (3) Deleted. <May 29, 2016>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 16-2 (Compliance with financial and accounting standards) The Veterans Association shall handle its budget or accounting in accordance with the financial and accounting standards prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 16-3 (Reporting of settlement of accounts) (1) The Veterans Association shall report the settlement of accounts under Article 10(2) to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs within the period prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs after the end of each fiscal year, along with an audit report on the results of the audit under Article 16-9(1).
  (2) If the audit opinion in an audit report attached to the report of the settlement of accounts under paragraph (1) is an adverse opinion, a disclaimer of opinion, or a qualified opinion due to a limitation on the scope of the audit, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall conduct an investigation or inspection under Article 17-2.
  (3) Based on the results of an investigation or inspection under paragraph (2), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall require the dismissal of an executive officer under Article 19(1) or take appropriate measures under Articles 30 through 33-3 of the Subsidy Management Act; and in such cases, the Minister shall, without delay, publicly announce the purport and reasons therefor.
  (4) If the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs determines that there is reasonable suspicion of a criminal offense based on the results of an investigation or inspection conducted under paragraph (2), the Minister shall file a criminal charge with an investigative agency.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

CHAPTER V-2 PROFIT-MAKING PROJECTS

Article 16-4 (Approval for profit-making projects) (1) If the Veterans Association intends to conduct a profit-making project referred to in subparagraph 6 of Article 4-2, it shall obtain approval for the project from the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs following deliberation and resolution by the Welfare Projects Deliberative Committee under Article 16-6.
  (2) If the Veterans Association intends to modify approved matters after obtaining approval for a profit-making project under paragraph (1), it shall obtain approval therefor from the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs; provided, if the Association intends to modify minor matters prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, it shall report such modification to the Minister.
  (3) If the Veterans Association intends to obtain approval for a profit-making project under paragraph (1), it shall satisfy all of the following requirements:
  1. The project shall involve a type of business and an item deemed suitable for operation by the Veterans Association, considering the Association's financing capacity, business operation capacity, investment scale, operational status of other profit-making projects, and other relevant factors;
  2. The Veterans Association shall have facilities, human resources, etc. for the profit-making project and shall directly produce goods or directly provide services;
  3. If any profits are generated from the profit-making project, such profits shall be used solely for the purposes of establishing the Veterans Association.
  (4) If approval for a profit-making project is revoked under Article 16-12(1), the Veterans Association must not obtain approval for another profit-making project for 1 year from the date of revocation.
  (5) The period of validity of approval for a profit-making project under paragraph (1) shall be 3 years from the date of approval.
  (6) If the Veterans Association has obtained approval for a profit-making project under paragraph (1) and intends to continue the project after the period of validity expires, it may, before that period expires, apply to extend the period of validity by up to 3 years. The same shall also apply to any further extension of the extended period of validity.
  (7) Matters necessary for the procedures and standards for approval for profit-making projects, the modification of the period of validity, and other relevant details under paragraphs (1) through (6) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 16-5 (Prohibition on lending of name) (1) If the Veterans Association has obtained approval for a profit-making project under Article 16-4(1), it must not allow another person to conduct such project in its name.
  (2) No person other than the Veterans Association shall conduct a profit-making project in the name of the Veterans Association.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 16-6 (Establishment of Welfare Projects Deliberative Committee) (1) The Veterans Association shall establish a Welfare Projects Deliberative Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Deliberative Committee") to deliberate on matters related to the operation of profit-making projects.
  (2) The Deliberative Committee shall deliberate and resolve on the following:
  1. Matters regarding the commencement, suspension, and discontinuation of profit-making projects;
  2. Matters regarding decisions on the scale of investment in profit-making projects, etc.;
  3. Matters regarding a plan for the use of profits or any modification of such plan;
  4. Matters regarding the results of an audit on profit-making projects and the appropriateness of such projects;
  5. Other important matters regarding the operation of profit-making projects.
  (3) The Deliberative Committee shall be composed of at least 5 but not more than 10 members, including 1 chairperson, and the following persons shall serve as its members:
  1. Two executive officers or employees appointed by the president of the Veterans Association;
  2. The following persons appointed or commissioned by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs; in such cases, no such person falling under the categories specified in items b through d shall be appointed or commissioned from among public officials belonging to the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs or persons belonging to the Veterans Association:
  a. One public official of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs;
  b. At least one attorney-at-law;
  c. At least one certified public accountant;
  d. Other persons deemed necessary by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, from among those with extensive expertise and experience related to profit-making projects.
  (4) The chairperson of the Deliberative Committee shall be elected from among and by the members.
  (5) When the Deliberative Committee deliberates and resolves on the matters specified in paragraph (2)1, the Committee shall consider the profitability, growth potential, and stability of profit-making projects, their impact on the market, and other relevant factors.
  (6) The Veterans Association shall operate profit-making projects following deliberation and resolution by the Deliberative Committee on the matters specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (2) and shall comply with such deliberation and resolution by the Committee unless there is a compelling reason not to do so; provided, if the Association holds different views on the deliberation and resolution by the Committee, it may request redeliberation as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  (7) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (6), matters necessary for the composition of the Deliberative Committee shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 16-7 (Operation of Deliberative Committee) (1) The chairperson of the Deliberative Committee shall represent the Committee and exercise general supervision over its business affairs.
  (2) If the chairperson of the Deliberative Committee is unable to perform his or her duties due to any unavoidable cause, a member designated by the Committee shall act on behalf of the chairperson.
  (3) A majority of the members of the Deliberative Committee shall constitute a quorum, and any resolution thereof shall require the concurring vote of a majority of those present.
  (4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), matters necessary for the operation of the Deliberative Committee shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 16-8 (Use of profits) (1) Profits from profit-making projects shall be used for the welfare of the members of the Veterans Association, operation of the Association, and the purposes of establishing the Association, with priority given to welfare projects for members.
  (2) The Veterans Association shall submit a plan for the use of profits for the following year to the Deliberative Committee and have it deliberated on no later than 30 days before the start of each fiscal year, and any modification of the plan shall require prior deliberation and resolution by the Committee.
  (3) If the Deliberative Committee determines that a plan for the use of profits under paragraph (2) does not conform to the purposes of the use of profits under paragraph (1), the Committee may present its opinion thereon.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 16-9 (Audit) (1) After the end of each fiscal year, the Veterans Association shall prepare financial statements and obtain an audit from a certified public accounting firm (referring to an accounting firm under Article 23 of the Certified Public Accountant Act that is designated by the Deliberative Committee; hereafter in this Article, the same shall apply). In such cases, a separate audit opinion shall be included for profit-making projects of a certain scale or larger, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  (2) A certified public accounting firm shall conduct an audit under paragraph (1) for the period prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs from the date of receiving a request for an audit and submit the results thereof to the Veterans Association. In such cases, the Association shall submit the results of the audit to the Deliberative Committee within 15 days after the audit is completed.
  (3) The Deliberative Committee may present its opinion on the operation of profit-making projects in consideration of the results of an audit conducted under paragraph (2).
  (4) If the Veterans Association has obtained an audit under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may instruct the Association to receive supervision of the audit report and the accompanying financial statements from a corporation or organization that has been entrusted with all or part of the supervisory duties by the Minister of Finance and Economy under Article 50(5) of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (5) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall require public officials under his or her jurisdiction to conduct an annual regular audit of profit-making projects performed by the Veterans Association under subparagraph 6 of Article 4-2.
  (6) Other necessary matters, including the methods of audit, the preparation of audit reports, and the procedures therefor under paragraphs (1) and (5), shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 16-10 (Fact-finding surveys) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may conduct a fact-finding survey of the operation of profit-making projects of the Veterans Association to ensure the sound operation of such projects.
  (2) If necessary for a fact-finding survey under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request the head of a relevant central administrative agency, local government, or public institution under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions (hereinafter referred to as the "head of a relevant agency") to submit materials. In such cases, the head of a relevant agency so requested shall comply therewith unless there is good cause.
  (3) Matters necessary for the methods of fact-finding surveys under paragraph (1) and other relevant details shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 16-11 (Disclosure of information and materials related to profit-making projects) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall disclose the following information or materials of the Veterans Association, which has obtained approval for a profit-making project under Article 16-4(1), on the website of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs within 180 days after the end of each fiscal year, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs:
  1. Financial and accounting materials prepared in accordance with the financial and accounting standards under Article 16-2;
  2. Materials related to the results of an audit under Article 16-9;
  3. Other information or materials prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs in relation to the current status of the operation of a profit-making project, etc.
  (2) If necessary to disclose information or materials under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request the head of a relevant agency to submit materials related to the Veterans Association, which has obtained approval for a profit-making project under Article 16-4(1). In such cases, the head of the relevant agency so requested shall comply therewith unless there is good cause.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 16-12 (Suspension and revocation of approval for profit-making projects) (1) If the Veterans Association, which has obtained approval for a profit-making project under Article 16-4(1), falls under any of the following categories, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may order the Association to suspend the relevant profit-making project for a period of up to 6 months or revoke such approval; provided, in the case of subparagraph 1, 2, or 5, the approval for the profit-making project shall be revoked:
  1. Where the Association has obtained approval for, or approval for modification of, a profit-making project under Article 16-4(1) or (2) by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where the Association has discontinued a profit-making project approved under Article 16-4(1);
  3. Where the Association fails to operate a profit-making project approved under Article 16-4(1) for at least 2 years;
  4. Where the Association fails to meet the standards for approval under Article 16-4(3);
  5. Where the Association has allowed another person to conduct a profit-making project in its name, in violation of Article 16-5(1);
  6. Where the Association refuses an audit under Article 16-9(1) or a regular audit under paragraph (5) of that Article or submits false materials;
  7. Where the Association refuses, obstructs, or evades a fact-finding survey under Article 16-10(1);
  8. Where the Association fails to comply with corrective measures under Article 17;
  9. Where the Association refuses, obstructs, or evades an investigation or inspection under Article 17-2(1);
  10. Where the Association refuses to submit reports, documents, or materials under Article 18 or submits false reports, documents, or materials;
  11. Where the Association conducts a profit-making project during the period of suspension of such project;
  12. Where the Association is subject to restrictions on qualifications for participation in tendering procedures under Article 27 of the Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party;
  13. Where the Association is subject to restrictions on qualifications for participation in tendering procedures under Article 31 of the Act on Contracts to Which a Local Government Is a Party;
  14. Where the Association falls under the category specified in Article 11(2)1 or 3 of the Act on Facilitation of Purchase of Small and Medium Enterprise-Manufactured Products and Support for Development of Their Markets.
  (2) When imposing a disposition of suspension of, or revocation of approval for, a profit-making project under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may allow the Veterans Association to continue performing duties under a contract already concluded in relation to the relevant profit-making project before receiving such disposition.
  (3) If the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs has allowed the Veterans Association to continue performing duties under a contract already concluded in relation to the relevant profit-making project under paragraph (2), the Association shall notify the counterparty to the contract of the fact and details of the suspension of, or revocation of approval for, the profit-making project under paragraph (1), within the period prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  (4) Matters necessary for the detailed standards for administrative dispositions under paragraph (1) and other relevant details shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 16-13 (Hearings) If the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs intends to suspend a profit-making project or revoke approval for such project under Article 16-12(1), the Minister shall hold a hearing.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

CHAPTER VI SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 17 (Corrective measures) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may order the Veterans Association to take corrective measures, in any of the following cases: <Amended on Mar. 4, 2023>
  1. Where it operates a profit-making project in breach of an Act or the purpose of its establishment;
  2. Where it uses profits in breach of its plan for the use of profits;
  3. Where violating an instruction under any statute or regulation prescribed by this Act or by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, or its articles of incorporation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Feb. 3, 2015]

Article 17-2 (Examination, inspection by administrative agencies) (1) When it is deemed necessary, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may have a related public official examine the accounts of the Veterans Association or review other necessary documents thereof. <Amended on Mar. 4, 2023>
  (2) In the case of paragraph (1), a related public official shall carry a certificate indicating his or her authority and present it to interested persons.
  (3) Deleted. <Jul. 11, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Feb. 3, 2015]

Article 18 (Request for submission of reports or materials) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request the Veterans Association to submit reports, documents, or other relevant materials regarding matters necessary for the enforcement of this Act, including approval for profit-making projects under Article 16-4, fact-finding surveys under Article 16-10, and disclosure of information and materials related to profit-making projects under Article 16-11.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 19 (Request for dismissal of executive officers) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request the dismissal of an executive officer of the Veterans Association, if such officer falls under any of the following; in such cases, the Association shall convene a general meeting within 60 days:
  1. Where the executive officer fails to comply with an order to take corrective measures under Article 17 without good cause;
  2. Where the executive officer causes a substantial impediment to the operation of the Veterans Association through disputes among executive officers, accounting fraud, or grossly improper acts.
  (2) A request for dismissal under paragraph (1) may be made only if the Veterans Association fails to comply with a request for corrective measures that the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs makes after hearing the reasons, within 15 days from the date of such request; provided, a request for the dismissal of an executive officer may be made without a prior request for corrective measures if it is evident that corrective measures cannot be taken even if requested, or in cases of substantial misconduct such as accounting fraud, embezzlement, or acceptance of bribes; and the detailed standards shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]
  [Previous Article 19 moved to Article 22 <Jul. 11, 2023>]

Article 19-2 (Suspension of performance of duties by executive officers) (1) In any of the following cases, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may suspend the duties of the relevant executive officer of the Veterans Association for a period of up to 60 days, which may be extended for an additional period of up to 60 days if unavoidable circumstances exist:
  1. Where an investigation or audit is in progress for a request for dismissal of an executive officer under Article 19(1);
  2. Where it is deemed that substantial damage to the operation of the Veterans Association is likely to occur if the relevant executive officer continues to perform his or her duties during the period of a request for corrective measures under Article 19(2).
  (2) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall immediately lift the suspension of the performance of duties by an executive officer under paragraph (1), if the grounds for such suspension cease to exist.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

CHAPTER VII PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 20 (Penalty provisions) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for up to 1 year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won:
  1. A person who obtains or causes another to obtain approval for, or approval for modification of, a profit-making project under Article 16-4 (1) or (2) by fraud or other improper means.
  2. A person who allows another person to conduct a profit-making project in the name of the Veterans Association in violation of Article 16-5(1) or who conducts a profit-making project in its name in violation of paragraph (2) of that Article.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 21 (Joint penalty provisions) If the representative of the Veterans Association, or an agent, employee of, or any other person employed by the Association or an individual commits any violation under Article 20 in conducting the business affairs of the Association or individual, the Association or individual shall be punished by a fine prescribed in that Article in addition to punishing the violator accordingly; provided, this shall not apply if the Association or individual has not been negligent in giving due attention and supervision regarding the relevant duties in order to prevent such violation.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 22 (Administrative fines) (1) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 5 million won:
  1. A person who fails to comply with the financial and accounting standards under Article 16-2.
  2. A person who conducts a profit-making project without approval under Article 16-4(1);
  3. A person who fails to obtain approval for modification under Article 16-4(2);
  4. A person who refuses an audit under Article 16-9(1) or a regular audit under paragraph (5) of that Article or submits false materials;
  5. A person who refuses, obstructs, or evades a fact-finding survey under Article 16-10(1);
  6. A person who refuses, obstructs, or evades an investigation or inspection under Article 17-2(1).
  (2) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 3 million won:
  1. A person who uses a similar name in violation of Article 2(4);
  2. A person who refuses to submit reports, documents, or materials under Article 18 without good cause or submits false reports, documents, or materials.
  (3) Administrative fines under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 11, 2023]
  [Moved from Article 19 <Jul. 11, 2023>]

ADDENDA <Act No. 1367, Jul. 19, 1963>
(1) This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
(2) As at the time this Act enters into force, the Korean Veterans Association shall be deemed to have been established pursuant to this Act.
(3) As at the time this Act enters into force, the officers of the Korean Veterans Association shall be deemed to have been elected or appointed pursuant to this Act in so far as it is not contrary to this Act.
(4) As at the time this Act enters into force, the articles of incorporation of the Korean Veterans Association shall be amended pursuant to this Act within two months from the date this Act enters into force, subject to approval by the Minister of National Defense.

  1. 다음 각 목의 개정규정은 2026년 1월 2일부터 시행한다. 다만, 부칙 제7조에 따라 개정되는 법률(가목 및 나목의 개정규정과 관련되는 부분으로 한정한다) 중 본문에 따른 시행일 전에 공포되었으나 본문에 따른 시행일이 도래하지 아니한 법률을 개정한 부분은 각각 해당 법률의 시행일부터 시행한다.
